page4.keyStrengthData: Competencies or behaviors where the individual excels, aligning strongly with the role's requirements and contributing to high performance.
page4.developmentNeedsData: Areas with gaps in competencies or behaviors, presenting opportunities for targeted training or support to improve fit and effectiveness.
page4.potentialRisksData: Possible competencies or behaviors that could hinder success if unaddressed, such as mismatches in work style or environmental preferences.
page4.untappedPotentialData: Emerging competencies or behaviors that can be leveraged for growth, offering paths for advancement and greater role contributions with appropriate development
untappedPotentialContent: Exploring and applying rules to specific problems

interviewSection.title: Providing Insights
interviewSection.description: Is focused on continuously improving things; provides insights by identifying key issues; makes intuitive judgments.

questions.question: Tell me about a time when you had to provide your insights in order to improve something at work.
subQuestions: How did you approach the task?
How successful was your approach?
How did your organization benefit from the changes?

questions.question: Explain by means of an example, what your approach was to getting to the key issue of a problem at work.
subQuestions: What was your approach to identifying the key issue(s)?
How did you know that you had or had not identified the core issue?
What if anything, would you do differently in the future?

questions.question: Describe a time when it was necessary to rely on your intuition alone when deciding on certain actions at work.
subQuestions: How often do you make decisions based on intuition alone?
How satisfied were you with your decision?
What changes, if any, would you make in a similar situation in the future?

interviewSection.title: Interacting with People
interviewSection.description: Is lively and projects enthusiasm; is talkative in making contact; is focused on interacting and networking with people.

questions.question: Discuss a situation where you had to work on a project at work that you perceived as exciting.
subQuestions: What was the situation/project?
Why did you find the project exciting?
How did you respond when you were informed about the project?
What if anything, did you learn about yourself?

questions.question: Describe a time when you had to make contact with somebody new and establish a working relationship.
subQuestions: Why was it important to establish this relationship?
How did you initiate the relationship?
Why was the first impression critical to the relationship?

questions.question: Describe a recent situation in which you had to engage with another person who you had not known previously.
subQuestions: What benefits were there for you to network with this person?
How did you develop this relationship?
How have you maintained contact?

interviewSection.title: Establishing Rapport
interviewSection.description: Builds rapport and puts people at ease; is engaging and welcomes people; finds it easy to make friends.

questions.question: Explain an occasion at work when you have had to build rapport and put people at ease.
subQuestions: What was the occasion?
What did you do to put the person at ease?
What did you do to earn that person's trust?
What was the impact of your action(s)?

questions.question: Give me an example when you were required to welcome people at an event at work.
subQuestions: Why was it important to welcome them?
What would have happened if you did not welcome them?
What was the outcome of your approach?
How quickly did you establish rapport with these people?

questions.question: Describe an occasion where it was beneficial to make friends at work.
subQuestions: How did you initiate the relationship?
What benefit was there in getting more acquainted with this person?
Why was the first impression critical to the relationship?
How did you nurture the relationship?

interviewSection.title: Convincing People
interviewSection.description: Is comfortable having to persuade others; shapes opinions by being outspoken; seeks to negotiate with others.

questions.question: Tell me about a time when you have had to sell your ideas to colleagues at work.
subQuestions: What was your approach?
What were your ideas that you wanted your colleagues to be convinced about?
Were you successful in persuading your colleagues?

questions.question: Tell me about a time when you had to convince people to accept your point of view at work.
subQuestions: How did you manage to convince the group individuals to accept your point of view?
What arguments did you use to support your point of view?
What was the outcome?

questions.question: Give an example when you had to negotiate with a client or service provider in order to get the best deal.
subQuestions: How important was it to negotiate?
What was your approach?
What options did you consider?
How successful was the process?

interviewSection.title: Articulating Information
interviewSection.description: Is articulate in giving presentations; is eloquent and explains things well; projects social confidence when articulating information.

questions.question: Describe an occasion where you had to present your findings of a certain project to a group of colleagues.
subQuestions: What was the topic of your presentation?
How important was this presentation?
How did you ensure that everybody understood the importance and impact of your message?

questions.question: Describe an occasion where it was important to communicate clearly in order for your colleagues to understand what is expected of them.
subQuestions: Why was it important to communicate clearly in this specific situation?
How did you ensure that your message was communicated clearly?
What other approaches could you have used to explain information even more clearly?

questions.question: Tell me about a situation where you had to display confidence while giving a presentation.
subQuestions: How did you cope with the situation?
What approach did you follow to convey your message in a confident manner?
What if anything, would you have done differently?

interviewSection.title: Thinking Positively
interviewSection.description: Is optimistic and positive; recovers easily from setbacks and obstructions; is jovial and projects cheerfulness.

questions.question: Describe a situation at work in which you faced a big challenge but remained optimistic and positive that you will succeed.
subQuestions: How did you manage to remain positive?
What was the outcome?
To what do you attribute the success / failure of the outcome?

questions.question: Tell me about a time when you have had to recover quickly from a setback at work.
subQuestions: What was the setback?
How did the setback affect you?
How did you remain optimistic and positive?
How soon did you recover from the setback?

questions.question: Tell me about a time at work when you had to present yourself as energetic and enthusiastic while emotionally you were angry or disappointed.
subQuestions: What led to your disappointment or anger?
Why did you have to project yourself as cheerful?
How did you cope with the situation?
What personal attributes did you use to cope with this situation?

interviewSection.title: Taking Action
interviewSection.description: Takes action to make things happen; uses initiative to start things up; shows drive and invests personal energy.

questions.question: Discuss a time when you had to take action and make things happen at work.
subQuestions: What was your role?
Why was it important for you to take action?
How did you go about taking action?
What did you learn about yourself?

questions.question: Describe an initiative you took at work without being instructed to do so.
subQuestions: What was the initiative?
What prompted you to take the initiative?
What did you do?
What was the outcome?

questions.question: Give me an example of a project that you led that needed quick action and implementation at work.
subQuestions: What was your role in taking the action?
What was the outcome of the project?
What if anything, would you do differently should you face a similar situation in the future?

interviewSection.title: Seizing Opportunities
interviewSection.description: Identifies business opportunities; creates additional sales for future growth; wants to win and outperform competitors.

questions.question: Tell me about a time when you used industry knowledge to identify a business opportunity.
subQuestions: How did you obtain the required industry knowledge?
What did you do to convert what you knew into a business opportunity?
How successful were you in this endeavor?

questions.question: Describe a time when you identified additional business opportunities for work.
subQuestions: What did you do to take full advantage of the opportunity?
What challenges and triumphs did you experience?
What was the outcome?

questions.question: Tell me about an opportunity you seized that resulted in you outperforming your competitors.
subQuestions: How did you find the opportunity?
What did you do to win the deal/opportunity?
What benefits did your organization gain from the opportunity you seized?

interviewSection.title: Technical Expertise
interviewSection.description: Develops and applies specialist and detailed technical or professional expertise; quick to acquire new knowledge and skills.

questions.question: How do you make sure that you keep your specialist or technical knowledge up-to-date?
subQuestions: How do you decide which are the most useful sources of information to refer to?
How do your efforts compare with those of your colleagues?
How do you ensure that you have adequate time to keep your knowledge current?
